findings.summary: Corpus rollback can be declared successful while the prior directive content was not restored: the proposed exact readback proves only identity presence and activity, but body-only directive changes reuse the same entry key and Qdrant carries no content fingerprint.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json exact_corpus_readback_contract defines corpus_get_identity responses as exists/is_active per store plus ACTIVE_BOTH/EFFECTIVE_INACTIVE/DIVERGENT_ACTIVE/INVALID; its rollback closure likewise requires prior identities active in both stores, without comparing manifested content.
src/memory_knowledge/workflows/corpus.py:45-58 states that body edits upsert in place under the same entry_key and that PostgreSQL and Qdrant are separate writes.
src/memory_knowledge/projections/corpus_writer.py:30-45 overwrites body_text and other fields on entry_key conflict.

src/memory_knowledge/projections/corpus_qdrant.py:30-43 embeds body_text but stores only entry_key, kind, link_slug, confidence, is_active, and content_kind; no body/content hash is available for exact readback.

A rollback interrupted after restoring the PostgreSQL body but before restoring the Qdrant vector can therefore leave both stores active under the same key; the proposed state oracle can classify that as ACTIVE_BOTH even though Qdrant still represents the forward body.
findings.correction: Extend the manifest and exact identity contract with a canonical content fingerprint covering the directive body and all projection-relevant fields. Persist that fingerprint in the Qdrant payload and return/compare the exact PostgreSQL and Qdrant fingerprints in preflight, forward verification, and rollback closure. Prior closure must require both stores active with the manifested prior fingerprint; forward closure must require the manifested forward fingerprint; any active-but-stale or cross-store fingerprint divergence must fail closed. Add tests for same-entry_key body changes and rollback failure between the PostgreSQL and Qdrant restoration writes.

findings.summary: Projection rollback does not restore target existence: adoption is required to create a currently missing AGENTS.md, but the rollback contract only regenerates prior directive content and never removes a file that did not exist before adoption.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json exact_topology.current_target_state records that the eighth trusted-and-allowlisted target is missing and requires create-missing; read-only inspection confirmed /Users/kamenkamenov/Documents/Codex/2026-07-10/can-you-assess-both-the-working/AGENTS.md is absent.
working-agreement/generate_projections.py:108-117 creates a new AGENTS.md when create_missing is enabled.

candidate-round-1.json research_markdown adoption/rollback text says to restore prior canonical and skill hashes, regenerate, reinstall, and resync, but defines no projection pre-state manifest and no absent-before restoration operation.

Regenerating the prior directives updates the newly created generated file; it cannot restore the prior state of nonexistence. Removing it later is destructive and must also satisfy the named-permission safety gate.
findings.correction: Add every projection target to the pre-adoption manifest with exact resolved path, prior existence, prior byte or generated-block hash, and forward-applied hash. Rollback must refresh prior generated content for pre-existing targets and restore absence for adoption-created targets only when the file still exactly matches the manifested generated artifact and deletion permission is present; otherwise it must stop for a bounded cleanup decision. Post-rollback validation must assert both content and existence parity for every target, including partial all-target apply failures.
